short_description: Experimental health-risk trait retained for research inspection of colorectal-cancer score behavior within the strict no-imputation raw-array workflow; it is not consumer-ready.
summary_note: Experimental non-consumer health-risk trait used to inspect how a bundled colorectal-cancer score behaves under the current strict raw-array workflow without imputation.
what_it_measures: A panel-relative polygenic signal associated with the bundled colorectal-cancer score, calibrated within the current local empirical reference panel for research inspection only.
interpretation_template: This is an experimental research-facing output, not a diagnosis, not a screening result, and not a clinical estimate of personal cancer risk. {interpretation}
caution_text: Experimental research output only. No imputation or ancestry-adjusted normalization is used, and the result should not be treated as a medical prediction, a screening decision, or personal cancer advice.
limitations: Percentiles and z-scores are relative to the local reference panel, not to a population-wide benchmark.
This trait is not consumer-ready and should stay in research review unless a separate product decision is made.
Real-world colorectal-cancer risk depends heavily on age, family history, screening history, ancestry context, lifestyle, environment, and many non-modeled clinical factors.
The current output is a strict raw-array polygenic signal only and should not be used to delay, replace, or reinterpret medical screening or physician guidance.
confidence_note: Confidence reflects overlap and reference robustness under the no-imputation raw-array workflow, not certainty about real-world disease risk.
reference_note: Percentiles and z-scores are calibrated against a local empirical reference artifact built from raw-array files in this project; they are panel-relative research values, not population-wide or clinical benchmarks.
